title: Bibimbap
skill: Each topping cut and cooked on its own, timed

notes.text: Cook each topping in batches no bigger than the recipe's, and fry the eggs two at a time.

move.title: Six toppings, one pan, in order
move.body: Bibimbap means "mixed rice": warm rice under separately seasoned vegetables, beef, and a fried egg, stirred together with gochujang at the table. Each topping is cut and cooked on its own in one pan. The skill is the order, written down as a timeline and run against the clock.

why.title: Light to dark in one pan
why.body: Cook the cleanest-tasting toppings first and the strongest last: carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, then beef. The spinach is blanched in its own pot. A quick wipe between them is enough, and the pan never needs washing.

why.title: Matchsticks cook in a minute
why.body: Carrot and zucchini cut into 5-centimeter julienne cook through in 1 to 2 minutes over medium-high heat, so they keep their color and bite.

why.title: Squeeze the spinach
why.body: Blanched spinach holds a lot of water. Squeezed hard, it takes the seasoning instead of diluting it.

why.title: Toppings wait; rice and egg don't
why.body: Seasoned vegetables hold at room temperature for the length of the cook. The rice stays covered and hot, and the eggs are fried last, so they reach the table hot.

wrong.sign: The toppings were cold by serving
wrong.fix: Cook the beef and eggs last, and serve straight from the pan.
Cook it on higher heat, in a single layer, for less time.
Squeeze it harder before seasoning, and taste after.
Note where. Cutting usually takes longer than you think; give it more time in the plan.

quiz.q: Which topping goes into the pan last?

choices: So it takes the seasoning instead of diluting it
quiz.explain: Blanched spinach is full of water.

quiz.q: Which parts must be cooked last?
How long do julienned carrots take?

substitutions.note: Same amount. Check the gochujang too; most have wheat.

steps.text: Write a timeline backward from serving: rice 35 minutes with resting, cutting 30, five toppings about 4 minutes each, eggs 5.
steps.tip: Run it against the clock and note where you fall behind.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear. Bring it to a boil with its water, cover, and cook on low, then rest it off the heat, covered.
Slice the beef as thin as you can across the grain. Mince the garlic. Toss the beef with the soy sauce, beef's sugar and sesame oil, and half the garlic.
steps.tip: Twenty minutes in the freezer firms the beef for thin slicing.

steps.text: Wash your hands, the knife, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Julienne the carrots and zucchini into 5-centimeter matchsticks. Slice the mushrooms thin.
Stir the gochujang, the sauce's sesame oil, sugar, vinegar, and water together in the small bowl.

Blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling water for 30 seconds, drain, cool under cold water, and squeeze hard. Season it with half the vegetables' sesame oil, a pinch of salt, and the rest of the garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in the skillet over medium-high. Cook the carrots with a pinch of salt until just tender. Move them to the plate.
Add another tablespoon of oil and cook the zucchini with a pinch of salt the same way.
Add the last tablespoon of oil and cook the mushrooms with a pinch of salt until browned.
Turn the heat to high. Add the beef with the tongs in one layer and stir-fry.
Wash your hands and the tongs.
Push the beef into a pile and check its middle. It needs to read at least 145°F.
Wipe the pan. Heat the eggs' oil over medium, crack in the eggs, and cover.
Slide the thermometer sideways into the thickest white. It needs to read at least 160°F; if not, cover 1 minute more.
Fluff the rice into four bowls. Arrange each topping in its own section, an egg in the center, sesame seeds over, and the sauce on the side.
steps.look: A wheel of colors around the egg.
